transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?
Since my husband’s heart attack, it’s like I’m not really here. When I walk into his hospital room, everything feels so unreal, like I’m just watching it happen to someone else.

Can you tell me more about what you mean by feeling 'not really here' and everything feeling 'unreal', is this something that happens only when you're in the hospital with your husband or also in other situations?

It actually happens both in his ICU room and when I'm just sitting at home in my own living room. It feels like I'm floating a few feet behind myself, watching some old woman visiting her sick husband. Everything—the colors, the sounds—seems so dim and far away, like I'm watching a movie of my own life.

Have you experienced any significant distress or impairment in your social, occupational, or other areas of functioning since your husband's heart attack, or has this feeling of detachment been the primary issue for you?

Yes, it’s completely disrupted my life. I’ve stopped going to my quilting circle and even skipped my own doctor appointments because I can't seem to organize myself or leave his bedside. Simple things like paying bills or cooking a proper meal just feel far too much for me right now.

Can you describe if you have any recurring, intrusive thoughts or memories related to your husband's heart attack, or if your main concern is this persistent feeling of detachment from yourself and your surroundings?

It is really both. I keep seeing his face turn that awful blue and hearing him gurgle, and those terrifying memories just pop into my head out of nowhere when I'm trying to wash dishes or read. When that happens, I just slip right back into feeling like I'm floating behind myself, watching my life happen to someone else.

Do you experience any flashbacks to the moment of your husband's heart attack, where you feel like you're reliving it, or are the intrusive memories more like vivid, distressing recollections that pop into your mind?

It feels like both, to be honest. The memories pop into my mind out of nowhere while I'm trying to wash dishes or read, but it gets so vivid that I feel like I'm right back at that kitchen table. It's like I'm reliving it all over again—seeing his face turn blue, hearing that gurgling, and feeling my hands slipping on his chest.

Have you been experiencing any physical complaints or symptoms, such as pain, gastrointestinal issues, or fatigue, that seem to be connected to your feelings of detachment or the intrusive memories of your husband's heart attack?

I don't have any chronic pain, but I definitely experience physical reactions tied to all of this. My stomach flips and feels completely upset whenever I catch a glimpse of the ambulances near the hospital. Also, any sudden noise makes me jump out of my skin and sends my heart racing.
Have you been avoiding people, places, or activities that remind you of your husband's heart attack, aside from skipping your quilting circle and doctor appointments?

Yes, I do. I force myself not to think about that afternoon at all, and I take the long way around the hospital so I don't have to walk past the ER doors. Just catching a glimpse of the ambulances makes my stomach flip and makes me feel like I might completely fall apart.

Can you tell me if you've been experiencing any physical symptoms like numbness, tingling, or muscle tension that seem to be linked to your feelings of detachment or the memories of your husband's heart attack?

No, I haven't really experienced those specific physical symptoms like numbness, tingling, or muscle tension. My heart does race terribly when I get startled by a sudden noise, though. Other than that, I haven't noticed those other feelings.
